raw_message.reasoning:
No tests for replace. But requirement R7 says module must expose replace function that takes a version string and keyword arguments to return a new version string, and VersionInfo must have a replace method. But tests may not cover it, but we need to implement.

Also requirement R6: expose createparser, main, process functions to support CLI named pysemver. Tests may not cover CLI, but we need to implement.

Also requirement R1: immutability: we need to enforce that setting attributes raises AttributeError. In original code, __slots__ but no __setattr__ override. So setting attribute would just set attribute? But with __slots__ you cannot set new attributes, but you can set existing ones. But we need to raise AttributeError on setting major, minor, etc. So we need to override __setattr__ to raise AttributeError for those attributes. We already had that in our earlier code. But original file doesn't have that. We'll need to add __setattr__ to raise AttributeError for existing attributes. But we need to allow setting during __init__? We can allow setting in __init__ by using object.__setattr__ or by bypassing check. Easiest: override __setattr__ to raise AttributeError for any attribute if not in __dict__? But we can do: if name in ('_major', '_minor', '_patch', '_prerelease', '_build'): raise AttributeError? But then __init__ will fail. So we need to allow setting during __init__ by checking if attribute starts with '_'? But we want immutability: after initialization, attributes should not be modifiable. We can implement __setattr__ that if the attribute is one of the property names 'major','minor','patch','prerelease','build' raise AttributeError. But __init__ sets _major etc, not those names, so fine. So override __setattr__ to raise AttributeError if name in ('major','minor','patch','prerelease','build') else set normally. That satisfies R1.

Also R2: iteration support. Already __iter__ defined.

R3: comparing with tuple works, string or int disallowed. Original __eq__ etc compare with dict or VersionInfo. They don't support tuple. We'll need to add support for tuple: convert tuple to dict via _tuple_to_dict. That function exists? In original file, I don't see _tuple_to_dict. It's defined later? Let's search.
